channel.title: INSIGHT BRIEF — Independent economics & investigative research magazine
channel.description: An independent research webzine that tracks the economy and finance, trade and raw materials, AI and tech, and disaster and safety through data and interviews. It is an independent media outlet, not a registered internet newspaper.

item.title: Overseas crypto card payment details will be reported to the National Tax Service in April 2027… Taxes are due in 2029
item.description: The National Tax Service reported to the National Assembly that it will secure retail payment details of overseas issued crypto cards through CARF's first information exchange (2027). Virtual asset taxation is being postponed until 2029, but CARF reporting will begin for transactions in 2026. We have summarized the timing of information exchange for each card issuing country and the overseas financial account and gift tax obligations that are currently applied regardless of deferment.

item.title: Enhypen set to headline Mad Cool 2027 as K-pop transitions to global festival dominance
item.description: On November 28, 2026, BELIFT LAB confirmed that Enhypen will perform as a headliner at Spain's Mad Cool 2027, joining a roster that attracts 200,000 attendees. Simultaneously, Twice's Jihyo becomes the first K-pop soloist to perform at the Vina del Mar Festival in Chile, signaling a shift in how global music revenue is structured.

item.title: The correlation between orgasm frequency and mortality: A critical health analysis
item.description: A decade-long study of 900 men reveals that those experiencing at least two orgasms per week saw a 50% reduction in mortality risk. Researchers now examine whether sexual activity is a primary driver of longevity or a byproduct of overall health.

item.title: The economics of a 2.4GW AI data center project and residential mortgage limits
item.description: As South Korea launches Asia’s largest 2.4GW AI infrastructure project, retail buyers face strict loan-to-value caps based on volatile property valuations. The 15 billion KRW threshold serves as a critical regulatory pivot point for financing.

item.title: Lukashenko challenges Putin’s territorial logic over Ukraine and historical claims
item.description: In a November 25 interview, the Belarusian president questioned Vladimir Putin’s historical justification for the war. The shift signals potential fractures within the alliance as geopolitical tensions impact global supply chains and trade stability.

item.title: Industrial fire response standards and the risk management of food processing facilities
item.description: A fire at a meat processing plant in Gwangju on November 28, 2026, triggered a Level 1 emergency response. Authorities contained the blaze within 26 minutes, highlighting critical challenges in industrial site safety and forest interface management.

item.title: A new gene-informed benchmark for validating pathology AI foundation models
item.description: Researchers unveiled a quantitative benchmarking framework on November 25, 2026, to bridge the gap between visual pathology analysis and biological truth. This system assigns 'BioScoring' to AI models to ensure clinical reliability.

item.title: High-tech security measures deployed for professional healthcare certification exams
item.description: On November 28, 2026, over 4,000 candidates faced unprecedented electronic surveillance, including radio wave detectors and full-body shielding, during national health professional exams. The initiative aims to modernize integrity protocols for medical licensing.

item.title: The December 9 Fed Hike Is 99% Priced. Here Is How Much of It Reaches a Card, a Mortgage and a Savings Account
item.description: Futures put a quarter-point increase at 99% for the 8-9 December meeting, which arrives with a new set of projections. Transmission is uneven: card and HELOC rates follow a 7.00% prime rate within weeks, a 30-year mortgage follows a 4.94% 10-year, and the average savings account pays 0.57% either way.

item.title: Financial stability measures and GDP outlooks signal a shift in 2026 economic policy
item.description: Financial authorities are preparing to deploy market stabilization funds as a proactive defense mechanism. Meanwhile, the central bank is set to revise its potential growth rate upward, reflecting robust semiconductor-led export recovery.

item.title: Basic pension of 380,000 won, three sections from April 2027… Couple’s reduction 20% → 10% condition
item.description: The amendment to the Basic Pension Act was passed by the Legislative Subcommittee of the Health and Welfare Committee of the National Assembly on November 25, 2026. The key is differential payment in three categories: 380,000 won for the bottom 30%, 359,000 won for the 30-45%, and 349,700 won for the 45-70%, and a couple reduction rate of 20% → 10%. However, the period from January to March 2027 is frozen, and the plenary session's resolution and section boundary notice remain.

item.title: The 40-year legacy of Sinchon Blues: Why human artistry triumphs over AI in the modern music economy
item.description: As the band celebrates its 40th anniversary on November 28, 2026, leader Eom In-ho warns that over-reliance on AI-generated music threatens the emotional depth of the industry. His perspective serves as a vital counterpoint to the automated content strategies currently sweeping Western streaming platforms.

item.title: The physics of power loss: Why 60% of U.S. primary energy fails to reach the grid
item.description: In 2025, the U.S. consumed 34 quadrillion BTUs of primary energy to deliver only 14 quads to end users. This 60% loss rate highlights a critical physical barrier to decarbonization and industrial energy costs.

item.title: Navigating the December 2026 housing market: A strategic look at the 4,215 unit offering in South Korea
item.description: As of November 28, 2026, 12 regional residential complexes are opening applications for 4,215 units. Investors must weigh local tax burdens and credit facility limitations against the scale of new supply in the 3rd new town developments.

item.title: Costa Rica bars UN Gaza rapporteur amid rising geopolitical trade friction
item.description: Costa Rican authorities denied entry to UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese on November 28, 2026. This incident coincides with intensifying US domestic pressure to reform tariff policies and global supply chain vulnerabilities.

item.title: Nighttime wildfire response challenges and the critical gap in emergency infrastructure
item.description: The November 27 wildfire in Sejong City highlights the logistical hurdles of midnight terrain navigation. With 36 personnel deployed, the incident underscores the disparity between regulatory staffing standards and the harsh reality of nocturnal disaster management.

item.title: Securing the AI frontier: Aim Intelligence wins top honors at the K-Digital Grand Championship
item.description: On November 27, 2026, Aim Intelligence secured the grand prize for its AI vulnerability detection technology. As high-profile cloud breaches hit the US Air Force and judicial integrity is compromised by AI hallucinations, the demand for robust security guardrails has become a global imperative.

item.title: Trump’s new overcapacity tariffs trigger cost shocks for US importers
item.description: The administration is imposing up to 20% levies on 14 trading partners to combat alleged overproduction. With cumulative tariffs reaching 45% for some goods, US manufacturers face severe margin compression.

item.title: Fed survey reveals reserve management strategies among major banking institutions
item.description: The Federal Reserve Board analyzed liquidity and balance sheet strategies from banks holding 75% of total system reserves. Conducted in September 2026, the survey provides crucial insights into how financial institutions navigate inflation and market volatility.

item.title: Black Friday ticket strategies and the data-driven economics of live entertainment
item.description: As of November 27, 2026, third-party platforms are leveraging discount codes to harvest consumer purchasing data. This shift transforms ticket sales from simple transactions into essential assets for measuring price elasticity and marketing efficiency.
